---
title: "Lab 09 — Mechanisms"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
social <- read_csv("data/social.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(messages %in% c("Control", "Neighbors"))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab09", title = "Mechanisms")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "The Neighbors effect on 2006 turnout is…",
  q2 = "An interaction means…",
  q3 = "This subgroup gap…",
  q4 = "Why is a larger effect among 2004 voters not yet the mechanism?"
)
```

## What you will do

Compare the Neighbors effect for two subgroups. A subgroup gap is not yet a mechanism. Download the `.txt`.

```{r gaps, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
social %>%
  group_by(primary2004, messages) %>%
  summarise(turnout = mean(primary2006), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Larger among 2004 primary voters (about 10 points) than among the others (about 7 points).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The same size in every household."),
  answer("Negative among people who had voted before."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("The treatment effect changes with the moderator.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The treatment caused the moderator."),
  answer("The average effect is zero."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Says where the assigned mailing had a larger average effect. It does not name the mechanism.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Proves that prior voting is the channel that produced the extra votes."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "The moderator was not itself randomly assigned as a test of one mechanism.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
